notes: Bug fixtures are the reverse of a QtTune fix commit (git diff <fix> <fix>^), so the diff introduces the bugs the commit fixed; the known bugs come from the commit's message and diff. Clean fixtures are forward diffs of commits no later commit fixed at the time of writing.
Each diff excludes tests/, docs/ and *.md, so the reviewer sees only the code the change touches and the diff stays under the input limit.

base_rev is the tree the diff applies to, and the fixture's repo_context.json is an index of it, built with --no-llm (purposes come from each file's first prose comment). post_rev is the tree the diff produces; score claims about surviving code against it, never against current QtTune.

Leak: the removed lines of a reverse diff carry the fix's own comments, which name the bug. A reviewer can read them. Quotes must come from post-change lines, so a blocker quoting them is demoted, but its claim may still be informed by them. Each bug fixture's leak field says what the removed lines reveal.
A known bug's symbols are what a blocker's claim about it names; the scorer credits a bug when a stored blocker's claim contains one of them. Read the claim before counting the bug found.

fixtures.subject: fix(j2534): clamp backoff step to the 5 s cap (#35)
fixtures.proposal: Inline the failure backoff step in the J2534 worker: drop j2534_backoff.h and double backoff_ms in place in all three worker modes, capped at J2534_BACKOFF_CAP_MS.

known_bugs.summary: The cap is checked before the doubling, so 3200 ms doubles to 6400 ms, above the 5 s cap; the next wait is clamped only after one overshoot.

fixtures.leak: The removed header's comment says the doubled value is what gets clamped so no wait exceeds the cap even though the cap is not a power of two times the base.

fixtures.subject: fix(j2534): ignore vendor message counts under hard-error statuses (#1)
fixtures.proposal: Simplify the J2534 read paths: take the vendor's reported message count as the number of frames delivered in both the in-process loader and the surrogate, and drop the qttune_trusted_count helper from j2534_ptypes.h.

known_bugs.summary: The loader trusts pNumMsgs whatever ReadMsgs returned; a vendor that leaves the count untouched on a hard error makes a zero-filled message read as a delivered frame and a healthy link.
The surrogate's read batch is static and never cleared, so a dirty count under an error status replays the previous read's frames as phantoms.

fixtures.leak: The removed helper's comment and the removed call-site comments explain both bugs, including the vendor observation.

fixtures.subject: fix(j2534): ?poll= overrides the profile's rotation instead of being ignored (#12)
fixtures.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

known_bugs.summary: sched_mode is true whenever the set has entries and the worker checks it before poll_pid, so ?poll= under a profile with mux defs is silently ignored and the URI's PID is never requested on its own.
parse_query rejects ?poll= without ?filter= before the profile's declared channels are known, so ?profile=obd2&poll=0x0C fails although the profile supplies the channel.

fixtures.leak: Removed comments describe finding 12: the precedence rule and why the channel rule moved to attach.

fixtures.subject: fix(bridge): start sessions on GUI thread; keep unsubscribed rows live
fixtures.proposal: Bridge connect: connectCoreOnly creates, registers and starts the session on the connect thread and hands it to the queued GUI completion through the lambda capture; drop the pending-session member and startSession. The signal model updates only subscribed rows, so the Live checkbox gates both the plot and the value.

known_bugs.summary: The session is started on the connect thread before the GUI thread has taken it, and the destructor knows nothing of a session whose queued completion was dropped, so a bridge destroyed mid-connect leaves a running worker calling onFrame with a freed `this`.
updateValues skips rows whose subscribed flag is false, so a signal unticked in the Live list stops updating everywhere, including the Dashboard gauges that read every row.

fixtures.leak: Removed comments explain why the session was not started off-thread and why values update regardless of subscription.

fixtures.subject: fix(bridge): honor payload length in signal decode and report drops from worker path
fixtures.proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.

known_bugs.summary: qttune_decode_signal is called with a hardcoded length of 8 instead of the frame's data_length, so short frames decode bytes past their payload and CAN FD frames lose signals beyond byte 8.
handleFrameInternal clears m_stagingBuffer before decoding each frame, so the coalesced batch carries only the last frame's signals and every other frame's values in the 100 ms window are lost.
Drops are counted in onFrame but reported only from handleFrameInternal, which does not run while the backlog is saturated, so the user is never told about drops while they happen.
payloadHex reads data_length bytes of the 64-byte inline buffer without clamping, so a transport reporting a longer length makes the bridge read past the buffer.

fixtures.leak: Removed FIX comments name the hardcoded length, the clear-and-refill and the worker-path drop reporting. The post-state is three commits after the bridge fixture's base, so this fixture reviews the same file as the bridge fixture, from the other direction.

fixtures.subject: refactor(core): ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown are optional no-ops
fixtures.proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.
fixtures.leak: None: a forward diff. Ten files across the app, QML and core layers; the layer note follows the first file (app/qml/HomePage.qml), a known limitation (backlog #8).

fixtures.subject: feat(bridge): log what each ECU supports
fixtures.proposal: Bridge: log what each channel's ECU said it supports, once per update, from the coalescing tick: the supported-PID count and range, and each request dropped from the rotation with its reason.
